title: CAMEO: A Co-design Architecture for Multi-objective Energy System Optimization
problem: Energy system co-design requires orchestrating heterogeneous components; monolithic solvers lack modularity
motivation: Complex interdependent optimization problems need flexible, scalable workflow framework
method: CAMEO breaks the energy system design problem into smaller, pluggable pieces that can run in any order as long as dependencies are met (using a DAG—a dependency graph where each node runs after its inputs are ready). Each component is containerized (packaged with its own software environment) and described using JSON specifications, so they can communicate with each other and be reused across different problems. Nextflow orchestrates these containers—it manages scheduling, data flow, and parallel execution—so designers can mix and match components without rewriting them.
key_novelty: CAMEO lets energy system designers solve different optimization problems by mixing and matching components with standardized interfaces, rather than building a custom solver for each problem.
contributions: Demonstrated on power grid, battery, and distribution network problems
